title: Typed-frame handshake: acceptance criteria, e2e tests, and developer playbook for schema negotiation and tool-call recovery
creator: Evan Tran
description: PRD-style acceptance ticket that consolidates requirements, edge-case tests, and an e2e verification plan for typed-frame streaming (frame-anchored JSON envelopes) and deterministic tool/function call behaviors. This ticket clarifies scope changes requested in the last PM sync: focus on schema negotiation, explicit handshake tokens for idempotent tool calls, client backpressure semantics, and an operator playbook for partial-emission recovery. The goal is to provide a single, executable acceptance checklist the runtime and SDK teams can use to sign off. It includes concrete pass/fail criteria, telemetry markers required by Console to attribute failures, and a minimal set of compatibility requirements for downstream parsers and gateway proxies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Handshake & Schema Negotiation: On stream start the server MUST emit an initial typed-frame with envelope header 'schema_id' and 'schema_version'. Client may request 'schema_hints'. If the runtime cannot honor the requested schema, it must respond with a 'schema_fallback' frame that lists the chosen schema and a 'compatibility_reason'.

2) Idempotent Tool Handshake: Every tool invocation must be preceded by a 'tool_handshake' frame containing a v4 UUID 'handshake_token' and a stable 'call_signature' calculated from canonicalized tool args. Replays with the same handshake_token must not re-execute side effects and must return an idempotent result envelope or a clear 'duplicate' indicator.

3) Partial Emission Checkpointing: The stream MUST include periodic 'checkpoint' frames at configurable intervals (default every 2s or 1024 tokens). Each checkpoint includes 'resume_token' that allows the client to request resume from the last committed checkpoint without re-running earlier tool calls. Resume must be possible even after a connection reset between client and server.

4) Error Modes & Repair Hints: If structured parsing fails mid-stream, runtime must emit a 'repair_hint' frame describing: error_class (parse|schema_mismatch|tool_failure), recovery_suggestion (retry|fallback_schema|manual_patch), and a 'trace_id'. Console/SDK must surface the trace_id and hint to the operator. Failure frames must be emitted before final stream termination.

5) Backpressure & Flow Control: The server must honor a 'flow_window' header from the client indicating number of tokens client buffer can accept. When 'flow_window' reaches zero, the runtime must emit 'backpressure_on' frames and defer non-essential batching until window is restored. Observable signals must be available in per-route traces.

6) Streaming & Finalization Semantics: Final frame MUST be a 'frame_end' envelope that contains an 'integrity_signature' calculated over the canonical concatenation of typed frames emitted (algorithm: sha256). If final frame is truncated, client SDK must indicate 'truncated=true' and allow automatic resume via 'resume_token'.

7) Compatibility: SDK parsers in Python and Node provided by DX must successfully parse 10k randomized example streams (internal fuzz corpus) with <= 0.5% loss of semantic fields and produce stable tool-call invocation events for operator playback.

8) Observability Requirements: Each handshake, checkpoint, tool_call start/complete/fail, and repair_hint must emit an event to the Console ingestion pipeline with fields: route, model_variant, shard_id, trace_id, handshake_token. Events must be queryable and correlated to token-level cost buckets.
9) Security & Privacy: Handshake tokens and resume_tokens MUST be short-lived (TTL <= 24h). Tokens must not embed PII. Ticket requires security review sign-off before release to production.

10) Performance: Under a synthetic workload that mimics 99th percentile user length distribution, aggregate added tail latency from typed-frame envelope processing must not exceed 8 ms per token on dedicated-1 instances compared to un-enveloped streaming baseline.
e2e_test_cases: TC-01: Simple stream - client requests schema v1.2; server responds with matching schema header; emit frames and frame_end. Validate integrity_signature and SDK parser roundtrip.
TC-02: Schema fallback - client hints v2; runtime cannot support v2; server emits schema_fallback; client accepts fallback; full flow continues. Validate fallback reason logged.
TC-03: Mid-stream tool failure - tool returns 503; runtime emits tool_failure frame with repair_hint and trace_id; ensure Console surfaces trace_id and operator playbook is attached.

TC-04: Resume after disconnect - stream emits checkpoint; client disconnects; on reconnect client uses resume_token to request remaining frames; runtime resumes without re-executing finalized tool calls.
TC-05: Idempotent replay - client resends a previously ACK'd handshake_token; runtime must return duplicate indicator and not re-run side effecting actions.
TC-06: Backpressure - client sets low flow_window; runtime emits backpressure_on; verify no message loss and batching deferred until window increase.
TC-07: Fuzz tolerance - run 10k fuzzed streams from internal corpus through Python and Node parsers; assert <=0.5% semantic field loss and no crash.

TC-08: Telemetry correlation - generate a multi-tool flow and ensure Console events include handshake_token and trace_id for each tool call; validate queryability and dashboard panels show correlated latency and cost per token.
TC-09: Security token expiry - issue resume_token with TTL=10s and attempt resume after expiry; runtime must reject and emit token_expired frame with recovery suggestion.
TC-10: Integrity failure detection - mutate a frame in transit (simulated); runtime and SDK must detect signature mismatch and emit repair_hint with manual_patch suggestion.
decisions: Adopt frame-anchored JSON envelopes (typed-frame) rather than ad-hoc interleaved JSON to simplify parser guarantees and integrity checks.
Use v4 UUID handshake tokens and short-lived resume_tokens (TTL default 24h).
Require telemetry fields in events (handshake_token and trace_id) to enable root-cause and cost attribution in Console.
SDKs will implement automatic resume logic with a single opt-out flag for non-idempotent client use-cases.
Security review is mandatory before GA; token design must be audited by Security team.
open_questions: Q1: Should repair_hint frames include an optional machine-readable patch delta (small diff) to enable automatic client-side repair? Pros: improved auto-repair. Cons: complexity and potential security surface.
Q2: What is the default checkpoint cadence for low-latency short streams? Is 2s/1024 tokens acceptable or should we adapt cadence to actual prompt length?
Q3: Should flow_window be an absolute token count or a relative percentage of client buffer?
Q4: Who will own the fuzz corpus maintenance and what cadence for adding new cases?
Q5: Are there any regulatory constraints for resume_tokens in EU customers (GDPR retention concerns)?
